hints.title: Split Point Decomposition
hints.text: For every split point j separating s1 = s[i..j] and s2 = s[j+1..k], the condition requires distinct(s1) == distinct(s2).

hints.title: Distinct Frequency Counting
hints.text: For a fixed split index j, count how many left substrings ending at j have d distinct characters, and how many right substrings starting at j+1 have d distinct characters.

hints.title: Frequency Product Aggregation
hints.text: Multiply the frequency of left substrings having d distinct characters by the frequency of right substrings having d distinct characters for each d from 1 to 26.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def countMagicalPairs(s: str) -> int:
    n = len(s)
    total = 0
    for j in range(n - 1):
        left_counts = [0] * 27
        seen = set()
        for i in range(j, -1, -1):
            seen.add(s[i])
            left_counts[len(seen)] += 1

        right_counts = [0] * 27
        seen = set()
        for k in range(j + 1, n):
            seen.add(s[k])
            right_counts[len(seen)] += 1

        for d in range(1, 27):
            total += left_counts[d] * right_counts[d]
    return total
```

complexity.notes: Iterating all split points with distinct alphabet tracking up to 26 letters.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: O(n^3) evaluation of all triplets (i, j, k) exceeds the time limit.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Fixed size frequency arrays of size 27 require O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Groups substring counts by number of distinct characters at split boundary.
